items.stem: Which of the following is the most important criterion for healthy community living?
items.answer: A. The chapter concludes that cooperative action, responsibility and positive values can help in improving the quality of life and healthy living conditions for one and all; kindness and harmony are among the values members develop in order to work collectively, and a community is said to be healthy when its members continuously work together.
grounding: A community is said to be healthy when its members continuously work together to maintain, improve and expand the available natural resources and avoid their wastage.
The example of Mawlynnong village shows that high income alone is not the only criterion for healthy living.
Cooperative action, responsibility and positive values can also help in improving the quality of life, and healthy living conditions for one and all.
In order to work collectively, members of a community need to develop values of co-operation, kindness, respect, gratitude, joy, peace and selflessness.

items.answer: D. The chapter needs all three: the community cannot depend solely on the government for safety, cleanliness, waste management and ecological restoration, a clean and hygienic India can happen only if members of every community cooperate, and the values of collective work nurture healthy social relationships - at Mawlynnong the people themselves sweep the roads, clean the drains and plant trees to restore nature's balance.
grounding: They are required to ensure rules and regulations for safety measures, cleanliness, ensure equal access of public amenities to all members, promote adoption of waste management practices, and help ecological restoration and conservation.

However, we cannot depend solely on the government to take the initiative. The quality of life in a community also depends on how the members of the community work to improve on available resources and ensure that the government provides for these facilities.

the vision of a Clean and hygienic India, once seen by Mahatma Gandhi, can happen only if members of every community cooperate and accept individual and collective responsibility of keeping themselves, their homes and their surroundings clean.
These attributes are important in fostering the principles of collective work and in nurturing healthy social relationships.
The people voluntarily sweep the roads and lanes, water the plants in public areas and clean the drains.
Trees are planted to restore and maintain nature's balance.

items.stem: What is your vision of a healthy community? Give at least 3 examples.
items.answer: A healthy community is one in which all residents have access to quality education, safe and healthy homes, adequate employment, transportation, physical activity and nutrition, and whose members continuously work together to maintain, improve and expand the available natural resources and avoid their wastage. Three examples of what that means in practice are: (1) access to basic amenities - regular water supply, safe drinking water and sanitation, and provisions such as electricity, hospitals, dispensaries, housing, roads and transportation, schools and recreational facilities; (2) cleanliness of our home and surroundings, with no open and unattended garbage dumps breeding flies and cockroaches and no stagnant water or open drains breeding mosquitoes; and (3) members who recognise their roles and responsibilities and work collectively, developing values of co-operation, kindness and respect.
grounding: A community is said to be healthy when its members continuously work together to maintain, improve and expand the available natural resources and avoid their wastage.
The healthy community only be develped when its members recognise their roles and responsibilities.
Healthy community is one in which all residents have access to quality education, safe and healthy homes, adequate employment, transportation, physical activity and nutrition.
Maintaining cleanliness of our home and surroundings is an essential feature of healthy community living.
Access to basic amenities such as regular water supply, safe drinking water and sanitation, is important for healthy community living.

Access to basic amenities also includes other provisions such as electricity, hospitals, dispensaries, housing facilities, roads and transportation, schools, colleges, employment, security, recreational facilities and so on.

garbage dumps are a potential breeding place for flies, cockroaches, insects and so on. Stagnant water and open drains breed mosquitoes, the carrier of diseases, such as, malaria, dengue and chikungunya.
In order to work collectively, members of a community need to develop values of co-operation, kindness, respect, gratitude, joy, peace and selflessness.

items.stem: A camping trip has been arranged by your school. Two girls from your community are not allowed to go for the trip. What are the points you would highlight to convince the parents on the importance of camping trip for girls.
items.answer: The points I would highlight are these. Camping gives students a good break, away from the monotony of the classroom, and an opportunity to learn from nature in a joyful, exciting and adventurous manner. Living in the natural environment with students from different areas, cultures, religions and backgrounds helps them learn to work as a team in various activities, and in this process students learn the importance of self-reliance, teamwork, co-existence, importance of natural resources and organisational skills. Camping also offers great opportunities for empowerment of the girls, which is exactly what the two girls would be denied. The adventure sport one can engage in while camping - trekking, river rafting, mountaineering, rock climbing and the like - helps to develop courage, self-confidence, leadership qualities and enhances concentration powers, and the evening campfires give a great opportunity for social bonding and for learning about different cultures through story telling, songs, dances, skits and games. The parents can be assured that these activities are conducted only in the presence of qualified and professional trainers, and that the essence of all camping activities is bonding with nature and the importance of living in a community.
grounding: Camping gives students a good break, away from the monotony of the classroom.
It gives an opportunity to learn from nature in a joyful, exciting and adventurous manner.
Living in the natural environment with students from different areas, cultures, religions and backgrounds, help then to learn to work as a team in various activities.
In this process, students learn the importance of self-reliance, teamwork, co-existence, importance of natural resources and organisational skills.
Camping also offers great opportunities for empowerment of the girls.
While camping, one can engage in adventure sport, such as, trekking, river rafting, mountaineering, rock climbing, repelling, paragliding, caving.
Adventure sport help to develop courage, self-confidence, leadership qualities and enhance concentration powers.
However, these activities should be conducted only in the presence of qualified and professional trainers.
During the evenings all may gather around campfires which give a great opportunity for social bonding.
Campfires also enable to learn about different cultures through story telling, songs, dances, skits and games.
the essence of all camping activities revolves around two main features
Bonding with nature
Importance of living in a community.
